source_review.notes: Checked foundational Cilk, MapReduce, LATE, Mantri, Hawk, tiny-task, Tail at Scale, and Borg publications plus current Java ForkJoinPool, Spark, Hadoop, Flink, and Kubernetes documentation. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product controls and semantics are attributed; the generic benefit model and operational recommendations state their assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed worker w, ready deque Q_w, task generation g, partition p, pinned identity i, assignment a, lease epoch e, attempt a_k, and winner W(j,g).
Reviewed surplus S_w, steal cost C_s, task duration T_j, primary remaining time R_p, clone delay L_c, clone runtime R_c, margin M, benefit B, confidence q, duplicate cost C_c, and headroom H.
Checked seconds, work units, item counts, queue slots, generations, epochs, percentages, and resource-seconds remain explicit where used.
Confirmed logical task identity is not conflated with attempt identity and exactly-one assignment is not mislabeled exactly-once external effect.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter keeps work-steal ownership notation separate from speculative-attempt and commit notation.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 remaining-time fixture and reproduced 7.5, 280.0, and 60.0 seconds plus selection of straggler and moderate.
Recomputed the compact example as primary 280 seconds versus clone 5+35=40 seconds, yielding 240 seconds gross benefit.
Recomputed Exercise 3 as 150-(12+80)=58 seconds and verified it exceeds the 20-second margin.
Checked Exercise 2 leaves six queued tasks after a four-item steal, enough to feed the victim's two slots under the simplified assumptions.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic examples intentionally omit uncertainty, interference, locality, fair-share opportunity cost, and external-effect risk; each omission is stated.

evidence: Derived B=R_p-(L_c+R_c) from the condition that a clone finishes before the primary and checked the strict margin rule B>M.
Verified the linear progress estimate v=d/t and R_p=(D-d)/v for positive elapsed time and completed work.
Verified a linearizable conditional queued-to-claimed transition admits at most one non-speculative assignment per item generation.
Verified a linearizable conditional winner install with generation fencing implies |W(j,g)| <= 1 while permitting multiple attempts.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter labels both ownership and winner arguments as conditional safety reasoning, not complete liveness or end-to-end exactly-once proofs.

evidence: Reviewed empty/all-busy queues, simultaneous thieves, one/many victims, tiny/coarse tasks, stale snapshots, ambiguous RPC, lease expiry, worker loss, and scheduler recovery.
Reviewed zero/unknown/nonlinear progress, insufficient peers, nearly complete primaries, heterogeneous partitions, skew, shared bottlenecks, and exhausted headroom.
Reviewed barrier gangs, priorities, residency, volume/state attachment, locality loss, draining nodes, bad hosts, and correlated failure domains.
Reviewed simultaneous completion, invalid fast output, scheduler crash after commit, lost cancellation, nondeterministic results, external effects, and late loser publication.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Safety, liveness, performance, fairness, security, and cost boundaries are treated independently.

evidence: Traced ready work through dependency validation, victim selection, atomic claim, lease/epoch ownership, execution, completion, and reconciliation.
Traced a logical task through primary/clone identities, isolated output, validation, winner transaction, downstream resolution, cancellation, fencing, and cleanup.
Checked resource, topology, residency, security, affinity, gang, priority, tenant, and fair-share eligibility survives both transfer and duplication.
Checked every attempt is charged and observable even when it loses, while downstream consumers resolve only the committed winner.
invariant_checking.notes: Cancellation is consistently treated as resource optimization; lease/generation and winner checks provide correctness fencing.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from pinned identity and readiness through stealing, speculation, publication, fault replay, and evaluation.
Checked the one-owner argument depends on one authoritative state and linearizable conditional claim, with separate liveness assumptions.
Checked the one-winner argument depends on validation-before-install, linearizable commit, durable recovery, and stale-generation rejection.
Checked the benefit argument explicitly weakens under prediction error, coupled resource interference, and uncertain startup.
proof_review.notes: Non-transactional effects before commit are explicitly outside the one-winner proof and require idempotency, transactions, a publisher, or disabled speculation.

evidence: Audited queued, ready, movable, stealable, claimed, assigned, running, speculative, completed, committed, cancelled, stale, and fenced terminology.
Confirmed stealing is not labeled duplication and speculation is not labeled a queue transfer.
Confirmed a slow attempt is not automatically labeled a consequential straggler and a different host is not automatically labeled independent.
Confirmed first process completion is not mislabeled first valid committed success and high clone win rate is not mislabeled net benefit.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Terms consistently name whether they concern work items, assignments, attempts, outputs, or logical winners.

evidence: Reviewed steal requests/success/conflicts/bytes, queue/idle time, clone launches/wins, duplicate resources, completion tails, fairness, cost, and cleanup metrics.
Confirmed no universal victim sample count, batch size, backoff, progress threshold, clone fraction, margin, confidence, or headroom value is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable fixture demonstrates arithmetic only and is not evidence for cohort validity, prediction accuracy, independence, or production benefit.
Confirmed production acceptance requires trace replay, controlled failures, shadow decisions, canaries, cross-tenant outcomes, safety gates, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter requires net outcome evidence and root-cause classification rather than treating mechanism activation as success.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the separation of queued-work redistribution from running-attempt duplication, then covered readiness, deques, victim selection, contention, eligibility, locality, ownership, straggler detection, remaining-time prediction, clone admission/placement, identity, commit, fencing, shuffle/effects, determinism, resource governance, diagnosis, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable claim/lease/request identities, bounded probes and batches, topology/policy filters, cohort construction, benefit/headroom gates, attempt-scoped output, winner records, cancellation telemetry, shuffle registration, effect publication, quotas, fault injection, canary, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from the central distinction and invariants through each control loop and its failure cases. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover stealing, contention, constraints, gangs, claims, stragglers, skew, shuffle, effects, executable estimation, arithmetic, protocol design, and production evaluation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Cilk/MapReduce/LATE/Mantri/Hawk/Borg researcher, Java/Spark/Hadoop/Flink/Kubernetes maintainer, cluster-scheduler operator, data-platform/SRE/security/FinOps specialist, affected tenant, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
